correctness.rationale: The proof correctly resolves all coprime progressions. The elementary criterion is that an odd prime \(p\) divides \(\varphi(m)\) exactly when \(p^2\mid m\) or some prime divisor \(q\mid m\) satisfies \(q\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(p\nmid A\), CRT and Dirichlet produce a prime \(q\equiv B\pmod A\) in any chosen nonzero, non-one residue modulo \(p\). If \(p\mid A\) but \(B\not\equiv1\pmod p\), any sufficiently large prime \(q\equiv B\pmod A\) works. In the remaining case \(p\mid A,\ B\equiv1\pmod p\), writing \(A=p^eC\), one chooses a unit class \(c\equiv u\pmod{p^e}\), \(c\equiv1\pmod C\), and \(d\equiv Bc^{-1}\pmod A\); Dirichlet gives distinct primes \(q\equiv c\), \(r\equiv d\pmod A\), so \(qr\equiv B\pmod A\) and neither \(q-1\) nor \(r-1\) is divisible by \(p\). The bundled verifier independently checks the construction for odd primes through \(19\) and all coprime \(A,B\le35\), but the theorem is proved by CRT and Dirichlet.
residual_risks: The proof is ineffective in the size of the least witness and is restricted to prime moduli.
